# Options and quick profiles

Every option of the in-app menu, as `settings.txt` keys (`/data/edenps4/settings.txt`, one `key=value` per line,
`#` starts a comment). The menu writes the file for you; an option set back to its default has its line removed,
so "default" always means whatever this version defaults to. A key written by hand that the menu does not
know is kept as it is. `env:NAME` is the line `env=NAME=value` (a driver environment variable).

The value marked **(default)** is what you get with no line in the file. Texts are the menu's English ones;
the menu also has them in Portuguese.

## VIDEO tab (video, GPU and speed)

| Key | Option | Values | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | Console mode | `handheld` **(default)**, `docked` | Handheld renders at 720p (lighter). Docked renders at 1080p (much heavier). |
| `resolution` | Resolution scale | `0.25`, `0.5`, `0.75`, `1` **(default)**, `1.25`, `1.5`, `2` | Multiplies the game's internal resolution. Above 1x is very heavy for the PS4 GPU. |
| `speed_limit` | Speed limit | `on` **(default)**, `off` | Off lets the game run as fast as it can (it may speed up). |
| `gpu_accuracy` | GPU accuracy | `low` **(default)**, `medium`, `high` | Low is faster (fewer syncs). High fixes effects in some games but is heavier. Medium is in between and exists only if this Eden has it (otherwise boot.log says so). |
| `reactive_flushing` | Reactive flushing | `off` **(default)**, `on` | Copies GPU data back when the game reads it. More accurate, but slower. |
| `async_shaders` | Asynchronous shaders | `on`, `off` **(default)** | Compiles shaders in the background: fewer stutters, but Eden SKIPS draws whose shader is not ready yet, so layers or effects vanish for a moment (seen in Super Mario Maker 2). Off is Eden's own default: the game stalls a little the first time and the picture is complete. |
| `astc` | ASTC textures | `cpu` **(default)**, `gpu`, `async` | CPU is the most stable mode on the PS4. GPU and async CPU are experimental. |
| `astc_recompress` | ASTC texture compression | `off` **(default)**, `bc3`, `bc1` | The PS4 cannot read ASTC: the textures are decoded and kept as RGBA8 (4 bytes a pixel). BC3 keeps 1 byte a pixel (1/4 of the texture memory) and BC1 half a byte (1/8, but alpha becomes all-or-nothing). The CPU does the compression, once per uploaded texture, and loses a little quality (gradients). Experimental: never tried on a console. |
| `shader_cache` | Shader cache on disk | `on` **(default)**, `off` | Keeps compiled shaders for the next runs. Turn it off only if you suspect a corrupt cache. |
| `dyna_state` | Vulkan dynamic state | `0`, `1`, `2` **(default)**, `3` | Level of the dynamic-state extensions (0 to 3). If the driver fails, try a lower value. |
| `vertex_input_dynamic` | Dynamic vertex input | `on` **(default)**, `off` | Vulkan extension. Turn it off if you get graphics glitches or hangs. |
| `vsync` | VSync mode | `fifo` **(default)**, `mailbox`, `immediate`, `relaxed` | How frames go to the screen. FIFO (on) does not tear. Immediate and Mailbox depend on the PS4 video driver, which may ignore them: if nothing changes, see boot.log. |
| `scaling_filter` | Window adapting filter | `bilinear` **(default)**, `nearest`, `bicubic`, `gaussian`, `scaleforce`, `fsr`, `area` | The filter that fits the game image to the screen size (it matters when the internal resolution is not the screen's). Bilinear is the default and the lightest; Bicubic, FSR and the others cost more GPU. |
| `anti_aliasing` | Anti-aliasing | `none` **(default)**, `fxaa`, `smaa` | Smooths jagged edges. FXAA is light; SMAA looks better and costs more. It costs GPU, which the PS4 has little of. |
| `anisotropy` | Anisotropic filtering | `default` **(default)**, `auto`, `2`, `4`, `8`, `16` | Improves textures seen at an angle. Default lets the game decide; 16x is the sharpest. |
| `dma_accuracy` | DMA accuracy | `default` **(default)**, `unsafe`, `safe` | Controls DMA operations. Safe can fix problems in some games but may cost speed. If unsure, keep Default. |
| `sync_memory` | Sync memory operations | `off` **(default)**, `on` | Keeps data consistent between compute and memory operations. It can fix problems in some games (Unreal Engine 4 is the most affected) but lowers performance. |
| `speed_percent` | Speed limit percentage | `50`, `75`, `100` **(default)**, `150`, `200` | Top emulation speed while the speed limit is on. 100% is normal; lower slows the game, higher speeds it up. |
| `async_presentation` | Asynchronous presentation | `off` **(default)**, `on` | Experimental. Shows frames from a separate thread (an Eden option, off on PCs): it may take a little work off the GPU thread. On the PS4 presentation goes through the video driver and the HUD hook, so it may cause flicker, repeated frames or hangs. Never tried on a console: turn it on only to compare. |

## PERFORMANCE tab

| Key | Option | Values | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `shader_preload` | Shader cache loaded at start | `0`, `128`, `256`, `1024`, `4096`, `all` **(default)** | How much of the game's shader cache is compiled before the game starts (about 32 KiB per shader). No limit is the default: the game keeps every shader it compiles, like Cemu, and nothing is deleted. A limit only saves memory: a cache over it is kept as vulkan.bin.bak (then .bak2, .bak3...) and a new one starts. If the app dies while the cache loads, the next start loads it with a single thread and, if that dies too, keeps the cache and starts empty. |
| `shader_notice` | Shader and memory notice | `on` **(default)**, `off` | Shows in the corner of the screen how many shaders are being compiled (like Cemu) and warns when direct memory is nearly gone. Also toggled from the L3 + R3 menu. |
| `driver_cache` | Driver pipeline cache | `on` **(default)**, `off` | The video driver's own cache file (vulkan_pipelines.bin). Turning it off saves memory and disk and rules out one possible source of crashes while loading shaders; shaders compile from scratch. |
| `covers` | Covers in the game list | `full` **(default)**, `thumbs`, `off` | Decoded covers sit in memory (up to 64 MiB) while the game list is open, and part of that memory may not go back to the system afterwards. Thumbnails only keeps just the small tiles; None decodes no picture at all. Applies the next time the app opens. |
| `hud` | Performance HUD | `off` **(default)**, `on` | Shows FPS, CPU cores in use, memory and temperature over the game. Also toggled from the L3 + R3 menu. |
| `hud_size` | HUD size | `normal` **(default)**, `small` | Normal or small (half the size). |
| `hud_position` | HUD position | `left` **(default)**, `right` | The top corner of the screen the HUD is drawn in. |
| `overlay` | Video overlay | `on` **(default)**, `off` | The video hook: HUD, L3 + R3 menu and colour swap. Turn it off if a game will not open and you suspect it. |
| `overlay_draw` | Draw the HUD and menu over the game | `on` **(default)**, `off` | Off keeps only the colour swap: the HUD and the L3 + R3 menu do not show. Use it to see whether drawing over the game causes a black screen or glitches. |
| `overlay_mode` | HUD and menu drawing (anti-flicker) | `keepalive` **(default)**, `classic` | Keep-alive holds the HUD, the notice and the L3 + R3 menu in every video frame and redraws them the moment the game paints over them: this is what stops the flicker (seen in Super Mario Maker 2). Classic is the 0.7.3 drawing: once per frame, it can flicker. |
| `overlay_poll` | HUD check interval (ms) | `1` **(default)**, `2`, `4`, `8` | Keep-alive mode: how often the app checks whether the game painted over the HUD. 1 is the firmest and uses a little more CPU; 8 uses less CPU and may let a frame through without the HUD. |
| `overlay_flip_stamp` | Also draw at the moment of the frame | `on` **(default)**, `off` | Keep-alive mode: besides the checks, draws the HUD inside the very call that shows the frame, so a frame the GPU already finished never goes out without it. Turn it off only to test. |
| `overlay_delay` | Wait before drawing the HUD (ms) | `0`, `1`, `2` **(default)**, `4`, `8` | Classic mode only: how long the GPU gets to finish a frame before the HUD and menu are drawn into it. If the HUD still flickers, raise it; if it shows late, lower it. |

## CPU AND MEMORY tab

| Key | Option | Values | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cpu_accuracy` | CPU accuracy | `unsafe` **(default)**, `auto`, `accurate` | Fast uses reduced-precision floating point (more speed). Auto and Accurate are more faithful and slower. |
| `multicore` | Multicore | `on` **(default)**, `off` | Emulates the Switch's 4 CPU cores on separate threads. Turning it off is much slower. |
| `vram` | VRAM usage | `conservative` **(default)**, `aggressive` | Conservative uses less video memory. Aggressive keeps more textures and may run out. |
| `memory_profile` | Console memory profile | `auto` **(default)**, `roomy`, `standard`, `tight`, `strict` | Picks the driver arena, the shader cache loaded at start and the driver cache from the memory your PS4 gives the app. Auto measures it (the System tab shows it); the others force a profile. Strict is the most frugal: it keeps every GPU image inside the arena (experimental). An arena, shader cache or driver cache set by hand to a non-default value wins over the profile. |
| `memory_action` | When memory turns critical | `warn`, `pause` **(default)** | The app watches the largest free block of direct memory (it is what runs out before a crash) and warns in the screen corner with the speed of the fall. Warn only shows the text. Pause (the default since 0.8.4) also pauses the game before the end so you can choose to continue, restart or leave (needs the video overlay on). |
| `sysflex_mib` | Game RAM in system flexible memory | `auto` **(default)**, `off`, `256`, `512`, `768`, `1024`, `1536`, `2048` | The PS4 has a second memory pool, the system flexible memory, which is not part of the ~4.5 GiB of direct memory that big games run out of. With this option the game's RAM uses up to N MiB of it before touching direct memory, so more direct memory stays free (see 'largest free direct block' in the log). The app tests how much the pool has and leaves 128 MiB to the system; if the pool is missing or refuses, everything stays in direct memory. Automatic (the default since 0.9.1) uses up to 1536 MiB. It worked on the console with 512 MiB; larger values have not been measured in every game yet. After a start that died before drawing, safe mode limits it to 512 MiB. Applies on the next game start. |
| `env:ORBIS_ARENA_MIB` | Video driver arena | `1024`, `1152`, `1280` **(default)**, `1536`, `1792` | Memory reserved for the driver (MiB). More avoids video-memory errors but leaves less for the game. With no choice here the memory profile decides (1280 on a PS4 Pro like the one measured); the System tab shows the value in use. Avoid 1024: a Super Mario Maker 2 start with it died loading the shaders. |
| `env:ORBIS_VRAM_GARLIC` | Textures inside the arena | `1` **(default)**, `0` | Experimental, last resort: keeps images in the driver's arena instead of extra memory. Uses less direct memory, but the driver warns it costs about 2/3 of the GPU speed, and it may be part of wrong graphics: if a game shows odd textures, try it off. |
| `skip_cpu_invalidation` | Skip inner CPU invalidation | `off` **(default)**, `on` | Skips some CPU-side cache invalidations during memory updates: uses less CPU (the PS4's weak point) but may cause glitches or hangs in some games. Experimental. |
| `cpu_clock` | Emulated CPU clock | `normal` **(default)**, `boost`, `overclock` | Experimental. The Switch CPU clock the GAME reads: Normal 1020 MHz, Boost 1734 MHz, Overclock 2040 MHz (Eden's values). It does NOT give the PS4 more CPU: it only changes the time the game sees. Games that cap their own FPS by time may run freer; others get fast audio or physics, or hang. Try it game by game. |
| `cpu_ticks` | Custom CPU ticks | `off` **(default)**, `1000`, `4000`, `16000`, `21000` | Experimental. Replaces the cycle count the emulated CPU adds after each stretch of code with a fixed number (an Eden option), which changes how often the game's threads return to the scheduler. Eden suggests 77 to 21000 and warns it may hang the game. Which value helps on this PS4 is not known: try one at a time and watch the FPS on the HUD. |

## ADVANCED tab

| Key | Option | Values | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bgra` | B8G8R8A8 colour fix | `auto` **(default)**, `on`, `off` | Fixes swapped red and blue in textures. If a game's colours are swapped (pink sky, blue ground), use Auto or Off. |
| `a2b10` | A2B10G10R10 fix | `auto` **(default)**, `off` | Fix for 10-bit textures, decided by a test at startup. |
| `rg` | R8G8 fix | `auto` **(default)**, `on`, `off` | Fixes swapped red and green in 2-channel textures. Auto decides from a test. |
| `swizzle` | Mapping self-test | `off` **(default)**, `test` | Runs a component-mapping test at startup. Diagnostics only. |
| `colour_swap` | Swap red and blue on the screen | `on` **(default)**, `off` | Swaps red and blue in the video output, so the blue sky does not come out pink. Turn it off if the colours are already right. |
| `profile` | Profiler in the log | `on` **(default)**, `off` | Records in boot.log where the CPU spends time. Useful for bug reports. |
| `auto_stub` | Use auto stub | `off` **(default)**, `on` | Fills in missing services and functions automatically. It can help a game that stops for lack of a service, but also causes crashes and instability. For testing only. |
| `region` | Emulation region | `japan`, `usa` **(default)**, `europe`, `australia`, `china`, `korea`, `taiwan` | The console region the game sees. Use your game's own if it complains about region or opens with the wrong language or content. |

## SYSTEM tab

| Key | Option | Values | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `language` | Menu language | `pt` **(default)**, `en` | Language of this menu's texts. |
| `menu_theme` | Menu colour | `blue` **(default)**, `green`, `purple`, `orange`, `pink`, `red`, `grey` | Colour of the menu: blue (default), green, purple, orange, pink, red or grey. Applies at once, and to the HUD and the in-game menu too. |
| `players` | Controllers (players) | `1` **(default)**, `2`, `3`, `4` | How many controllers the game is given, 1 to 4. Player 1's controller is the usual one. Players 2 to 4 are the other users logged in to the console: turn on the second DualShock, press the PS button and join as a guest; the app looks every 2 seconds and lights the controller (red, green, pink). With 1 (the default) nothing changes. The in-game menu (L3 + R3) stays with controller 1 only. Applies on the next game start. The Eden-side connection has not been tested on the console yet. |

## Quick profiles

The first row of the VIDEO tab sets several options at once, to try combinations fast. They do not promise
that a game will open. Options a profile does not name go back to their defaults.

| Profile | Sets | What it is for |
|---|---|---|
| Default | (nothing: every option at its default) | Every video and CPU option at this version's values. |
| Light (more speed) | `bgra=auto`, `resolution=0.75`, `gpu_accuracy=low`, `reactive_flushing=off`, `async_shaders=on`, `astc=cpu`, `vram=conservative` | 0.75x resolution, low GPU accuracy, no reactive flushing, async shaders, ASTC on the CPU and conservative VRAM. Less quality, more speed. |
| Compatibility (more faithful) | `bgra=auto`, `gpu_accuracy=high`, `reactive_flushing=on`, `cpu_accuracy=auto`, `dyna_state=0`, `vertex_input_dynamic=off`, `async_shaders=off` | High GPU accuracy, reactive flushing, auto CPU accuracy, no dynamic state or dynamic vertex input, synchronous shaders. Slower, uses fewer risky driver extensions. |
| Save RAM | `resolution=0.75`, `env:ORBIS_ARENA_MIB=1152`, `vram=conservative`, `shader_preload=1024`, `driver_cache=off`, `astc=cpu`, `memory_profile=tight`, `memory_action=pause` | 0.75x resolution, 1152 MiB video arena, conservative VRAM, shader cache loaded up to ~32 MiB (what is over is kept, not deleted), no driver cache, the tight memory profile and a pause when memory turns critical. Less memory used, for games that do not open or hang for lack of it. |
| More video memory | `env:ORBIS_ARENA_MIB=1792` | 1792 MiB video arena. Less memory is left for the game: use it if video-memory errors show up. |
| Exact graphics (test) | `gpu_accuracy=high`, `reactive_flushing=on`, `dma_accuracy=safe`, `sync_memory=on`, `async_shaders=off`, `env:ORBIS_VRAM_GARLIC=1` | For wrong graphics (blurred or flat textures, as in Super Mario Maker 2's themes): high GPU accuracy, reactive flushing, safe DMA, synchronised memory, synchronous shaders and textures back outside the driver's arena. Slower. The cause is not confirmed yet; it is for comparing with the other profiles. |
| More FPS (test) | `resolution=0.75`, `gpu_accuracy=low`, `reactive_flushing=off`, `sync_memory=off`, `skip_cpu_invalidation=on`, `async_presentation=on`, `anti_aliasing=none`, `anisotropy=default`, `scaling_filter=bilinear`, `astc=cpu` | For CPU-bound games (Super Mario Maker 2's case): 0.75x resolution, low GPU accuracy, no reactive flushing or synchronised memory, skips inner CPU invalidations and shows frames from a separate thread. No extra filters. It does not promise more FPS: a light GPU helps little when the CPU is the limit. If the game hangs while opening, safe mode turns the experimental parts off for the next start. |
| Minimum RAM (test) | `resolution=0.5`, `env:ORBIS_ARENA_MIB=1152`, `vram=conservative`, `shader_preload=256`, `driver_cache=off`, `astc=cpu`, `astc_recompress=bc3`, `memory_profile=tight`, `memory_action=pause`, `covers=thumbs`, `sysflex_mib=2048` | The most frugal setting that does not make the game too ugly: 0.5x resolution (GPU images, which live outside the arena, take a quarter), ASTC textures kept as BC3 (1/4 of the memory), 1152 MiB video arena, conservative VRAM, shader cache loaded up to ~8 MiB (what is over is kept, not deleted), no driver cache, the tight memory profile, a pause when memory turns critical and the game list with thumbnails only, and the game's RAM uses up to 2048 MiB of the system flexible memory (what the pool has, less 128 MiB; an idea from Eden4). The picture gets much softer. |

54 options, 8 profiles.
